# expo-mediapipe-pose

> Community on-device pose landmarks for Expo and React Native, using Google's MediaPipe Pose Landmarker. Not an official Google or Expo package.

The app reads named joints such as `landmarks.leftWrist`. The package draws the skeleton. Live camera, photo, and video all return a `PoseFrame`. Expo Go is unsupported. Use a development build.

Install `expo-mediapipe-pose` and peer `react-native-svg`. The three pose models (lite, full, heavy) are bundled. Full is the default.

## Start here

- [README](https://github.com/YosefHayim/expo-mediapipe-pose/blob/main/README.md): Install, permission, camera, landmarks, skeleton, photo, video, models, and failures.
- [Show a pose camera](https://github.com/YosefHayim/expo-mediapipe-pose/blob/main/README.md#show-a-pose-camera): `requestCameraPermission` once, then `PoseCameraView`.
- [Camera permission](https://github.com/YosefHayim/expo-mediapipe-pose/blob/main/README.md#camera-permission): Config plugin sentence, then one runtime dialog.
- [Named landmarks](https://github.com/YosefHayim/expo-mediapipe-pose/blob/main/README.md#named-landmarks): 33 names, null when missing, world landmarks in meters.
- [Photo and video](https://github.com/YosefHayim/expo-mediapipe-pose/blob/main/README.md#photo-and-video): `readPosePhoto` and `readPoseVideo`.
- [Failures](https://github.com/YosefHayim/expo-mediapipe-pose/blob/main/README.md#failures): `onPoseFailure` reasons. An empty pose is not a failure.

Pose index is not a person id. Do not infer device performance or medical accuracy from a successful build.
